For each integer \(n\ge2\), let \(F_n\) be the free group on \(n\) generators. For any group \(G\), define its lower central series by \(\gamma_1(G)=G\) and \(\gamma_{r+1}(G)=[\gamma_r(G),G]\), where \([H,K]\) is the subgroup generated by the commutators \([h,k]=hkh^{-1}k^{-1}\) with \(h\in H\) and \(k\in K\). For every integer \(r\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal A_r(n)=\ker\!\left(\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}\bigl(F_n/\gamma_{r+1}(F_n)\bigr)\right),
\qquad \operatorname{IA}_n=\mathcal A_1(n).
\]
Determine, by explicit conditions on \(n\) and \(c\), the complete set
\[
\mathcal D=\left\{(n,c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:\ 
\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subsetneq
\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)
\right\}.
\]

This asks for a classification that is **not currently known**: it is a graded form of the Andreadakis problem.

To see the connection, put \(H=F_n/\gamma_2(F_n)\). The degree-\(c\) Johnson homomorphism restricts to a map
\[
J_c:\frac{\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)}
{\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)}
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}
\left(H,\frac{\gamma_{c+1}(F_n)}{\gamma_{c+2}(F_n)}\right).
\]
Here one uses the standard inclusion
\(\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_c(n)\).
Its kernel is exactly
\[
\ker J_c=
\frac{\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)}
{\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
(n,c)\in\mathcal D\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad J_c
\text{ is not injective}.
\]
The noninjectivity degrees of these maps have not been completely classified.

Some established facts illustrate the situation:

* **Rank two:** \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\), and its lower central series agrees with the Andreadakis filtration. Thus
  \[
  (2,c)\notin\mathcal D\qquad(c\ge1).
  \]
* **Degree one:** the abelianization theorem for \(\operatorname{IA}_n\) gives
  \[
  \mathcal A_2(n)=[\operatorname{IA}_n,\operatorname{IA}_n],
  \]
  so \((n,1)\notin\mathcal D\).
* **A known counterexample:** Bartholdi’s rank-three computation gives a nonzero degree-six kernel, yielding
  \[
  (3,6)\in\mathcal D.
  \]

Moreover, if for a fixed \(n\) none of the pairs \((n,c)\) belonged to \(\mathcal D\), induction would give
\(\mathcal A_c(n)=\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\) for every \(c\): whenever equality holds at degree \(c\), absence from \(\mathcal D\) gives equality at degree \(c+1\).

Thus the requested complete explicit conditions go beyond the known results:
\[
\boxed{\text{A complete determination of }\mathcal D\text{ is an open problem.}}

The team established the proposed answer:
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D=\{(n,c):n\ge3,\ c\ge3\}.}
\]
Their proof uses explicitly declared structural theorems, not Python alone. In particular, they **invoke rather than reprove** integral degree-two Johnson injectivity, and standard results of Magnus, Nielsen, Matsumoto, Bass–Heller–Swan, and local reciprocity. They did not obtain a verified bibliographic citation for the integral Johnson theorem and deliberately avoided attributing it incorrectly.

No finding contradicts the proposed answer. Several early approaches failed, but an eventual stable metaplectic detector supplied strictness for all required ranks and degrees.

## General reduction and equality cases

Strong centrality,
\[
[\mathcal A_r(n),\mathcal A_s(n)]\subseteq\mathcal A_{r+s}(n),
\]
gives \(\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_c(n)\). The degree-\(c\) Johnson homomorphism therefore induces
\[
\tau_c:\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(H,L_{c+1}(H)).
\]
The required strictness is exactly noninjectivity of this map. General reduction notes are in `workspace/agent1_general_reduction.txt`.

* **\(c=1\), all \(n\):** Magnus generators have first Johnson images forming the signed standard basis of \(H^*\otimes\Lambda^2H\). Since they generate \(\operatorname{IA}_n\), its abelianization is precisely this free abelian group. Thus
  \[
  \mathcal A_2(n)=\gamma_2(\operatorname{IA}_n).
  \]

* **\(c=2\), all \(n\):** The proof invokes the classical **integral** statement
  \[
  \tau_2:\gamma_2(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_n)
  \hookrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H,L_3(H)).
  \]

* **\(n=2\), every \(c\):** An explicit Nielsen-generator calculation gives \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\). The free-Lie centralizer argument gives

\[
K_{12}:x_1\mapsto x_2x_1x_2^{-1},\qquad
C_{i;jk}:x_i\mapsto[x_j,x_k]x_i,
\]

\[
w_c=[D,[A,\operatorname{ad}_D^{\,c-3}B]],
\qquad \operatorname{ad}_D(g)=[D,g].
\]
Certainly \(w_c\in\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\).

Its initial Johnson derivation vanishes integrally. Writing \(X=X_1,Y=X_2,Z=X_3\) and \(T=\operatorname{ad}Y\), the relevant derivations are
\[
D(X)=TX,\qquad A(X)=TZ,\qquad B(Z)=-TX.
\]
The derivation \(\operatorname{ad}_D^kB\) sends \(Z\) to \(-T^{k+1}X\); its bracket with \(A\) is diagonal on \(X,Z\), with entries \(T^{k+2},-T^{k+2}\), and commutes with \(D\). Therefore
\[
w_c\in\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n).
\]

The difficult step was proving \(w_c\notin\gamma_{c+1}\), uniformly in \(n\).

## Stable detector

Take the character \(F_n\to\mathbb Z\) sending \(x_2\) to \(1\) and all other generators to \(0\). Its kernel’s abelianization is a free module over
\[
R=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]
\]
of rank \(n-1\), giving an honest Alexander representation of \(\operatorname{IA}_n\).

In the final **column convention**, with \(s=t-1\), the relevant matrices are
\[
D=\operatorname{diag}(t,1),\quad A=E_{21}(s),\quad B=E_{12}(-s).
\]
Exactly,
\[
\operatorname{ad}_D^kB=E_{12}(-s^{k+1}).
\]
Gaussian factorization of the inner commutator has torus parameter \(1+s^{c-1}\), with remaining root factors of depth at least \(c\).

Balance determinants using an auxiliary coordinate and pass to stable elementary matrices. Bass–Heller–Swan gives
\[
K_2(R)\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^2,
\]
generated by \(\{-1,-1\}\) and \(\{-1,t\}\). Consequently specialization into a suitable local-field Hilbert-symbol cover descends to a genuine homomorphism: odd-order Hilbert symbols kill this kernel; for quadratic symbols, choose a field containing \(i\).

For an odd prime \(p\mid c\), take the totally ramified field defined by
\[
\Phi_p(1+\pi^{c/p})=0.
\]
For powers of two \(c\ge4\), use
\[
\pi^{c/2}-2\pi^{c/4}+2=0.
\]
These have residue field \(\mathbb F_p\), contain \(\mu_p\), and satisfy \(pe/(p-1)=c\). Critical local unit pairing gives
\[

\]

## Main conclusion: the supplied answer is contradicted

The team ultimately proved

(3,3)\in\mathcal D,

### 1. The counterexample

Write \(F_3=\langle x,y,z\rangle\). Define automorphisms fixing generators not explicitly mentioned:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
a:x\mapsto yxy^{-1},& b:x\mapsto zxz^{-1},\\
m:x\mapsto [y,z]x,& d:y\mapsto xyx^{-1},\\
e:y\mapsto [x,z]y.&
\end{array}
\]
All belong to \(\operatorname{IA}_3\). With the problem’s commutator convention, put
\[
u=[ [a,e],m]^3
  [[a,m],e]^{-1}
  [[a,b],b]^{-4}
  [[b,m],d]^{-2}.
\]
Plainly \(u\in\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_3)\). The team proved
\[
u\in\mathcal A_4(3),\qquad
u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3).
\]

### 2. Why \(u\in\mathcal A_4(3)\)

The standard central-filtration property gives
\(\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_r(n)\). The degree-\(r\) Johnson map records the action modulo \(\mathcal A_{r+1}\), with values in degree-\(r\) derivations of the free Lie ring; it respects brackets.

Number the relevant Magnus generators as
\[
(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3,g_5)=(a,b,m,d,e),
\]
and let \(D_{ijk}=[[D_i,D_j],D_k]\), where \(D_i\) is the first Johnson derivation. The exact integral identity is
\[
3D_{052}-D_{025}-4D_{011}-2D_{123}=0.
\]
It is precisely the degree-three Johnson image of \(u\).

A short hand verification was obtained. In the free Lie ring set
\[
k=[x,y],\quad w=[y,z],\quad h=[x,z],
\]
\[
P=[[k,z],z],\quad Q=[[w,z],x],\quad
R=[w,h],\quad S=[[h,z],y],\quad T=[[w,y],z].
\]
The derivations \(D_{052},D_{025},D_{011},D_{123}\), listed by their values on \((x,y,z)\), are respectively
\[
(-P+Q-R,T,0),\quad(-S-R,T,0),\quad
(Q,0,0),\quad(-P,T,0).
\]
Jacobi and Leibniz give \(S=P+Q+2R\), proving the identity.

Independently, literal substitution of the **92 signed Magnus generators** comprising \(u\), over the integers in truncated noncommutative Magnus series, fixed every generator through degree four. Thus this check concerned the actual automorphism, not merely tangent vectors.

### 3. Why \(u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3)\)

They constructed a genuine homomorphism
\[
\operatorname{IA}_3\longrightarrow
H\longrightarrow \operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb F_2),
\]
where
\[
H\cong C_2*C_2*C_2=\langle A,B,C\mid A^2=B^2=C^2=1\rangle.
\]

For the first map, take the abelianized Fox Jacobian evaluated at all variables \(-1\). **Convention matters:** row Jacobians are antihomomorphisms, so use the Jacobian of the inverse automorphism. These matrices fix \((1,1,1)\); quotienting by that vector and projectivizing gives a level-two subgroup of \(\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb Z)\).

The whole projective level-two subgroup is generated by
\[
A(z)=-z,\qquad B(z)=2-z,\qquad C(z)=\frac z{2z-1}.
\]
Containment for the entire IA group—not just the displayed generators—was audited. An even-Euclidean-algorithm argument proves generation. Ping-pong on
\[
(-\infty,0),\quad(1,\infty),\quad(0,1)
\]
proves the free-product presentation. The five automorphism images are
\[
(a,b,m,d,e)\mapsto(B,A,AB,C,AC).
\]

Now map
\[
A\mapsto I+E_{12},\qquad
B\mapsto I+E_{34},\qquad
C\mapsto I+E_{23}.
\]
In this target, the three correction commutators in \(u\) are trivial, while
\[
[[B,AC],AB]=I+E_{14}.
\]
Consequently \(u\mapsto I+E_{14}\ne I\). Since \(\operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb F_2)\) has class three, \(\gamma_4\) maps trivially. This proves the counterexample.

## Other established results

* **Formal reduction:** the defect in the question is the kernel of the integral graded Johnson map
  \[
  \gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
  \longrightarrow\operatorname{Der}_c(L_n).
  \]

  \(Z(F_2/\gamma_{r+1})=\gamma_r/\gamma_{r+1}\). The latter follows from the common-centralizer argument in the free associative algebra.

  \(\operatorname{Hom}(H,\Lambda^2H)\), proving \(\mathcal A_2=\gamma_2\).

* **Rank three, all \(c\ge3\):** the reflection-algebra detector gives propagation. The cubic witness has leading polynomial
  \[
  ACB+CAB+BAC+BCA
  \]
  in \(\mathbb F_2\langle A,B,C\rangle/(A^2,B^2,C^2)\). Successive brackets appending \(C,B,C,B,\ldots\) preserve the coefficient of the word beginning \(ACB\). Hence nonzero Johnson-kernel classes occur in every subsequent degree.

The principal reproducible files are:

* `workspace/agent1_cubic_direct.py`
* `workspace/agent3_cubic_independent.py` — independent source, Fox-target, and finite-target checks.
* `workspace/agent4_degree3_direct.py`

* `workspace/agent1_degree1.py` — degree-one checks.
* `workspace/agent4_rank3.md`, `agent4_seed_verify.py`, `agent3_propagation.md` — earlier quartic seed and propagation.

They did **not** determine the actual complete set \(\mathcal D\). General-rank \(c=2,3\) and strictness for \(n\ge4\) remain unresolved. Reported integral \(c=2\) certificates cover \(n=3,\ldots,6\), using true-relator lattices with unit pivots (`agent2_c2_hnf.py`, associated relation JSON files); the proposed all-rank support reduction was withdrawn.

Above the principal congruence subgroup \(\Gamma_1\), quotient by the canonically split subgroup above \(\Gamma_{c+1}\). The resulting group \(Q\) is nilpotent of class at most \(c\), and its central \(\mu_p\) survives injectively.

For completeness, the filtration assertion follows from root and torus collection. Local reciprocity gives
\[
(U_r,U_s)_p=1\quad(r+s>c),
\qquad U_{c+1}\subseteq K^{*p},
\]
where \(U_r=1+\pi^r\mathcal O_K\). Nonopposite-root commutators multiply parameters; torus-root commutators add depths; torus-torus discrepancies are Hilbert symbols. Opposite-root collection introduces symbols whose first argument is \(1+ab\). These vanish whenever the total depth exceeds \(c\). Thus the deep splitting is normal and
\([F_r,F_s]\subseteq F_{r+s}\), proving the stated nilpotency bound.

The Alexander representation lifts to this cover after balancing its determinant by an extra coordinate. Indeed, Bass–Heller–Swan gives
\[
\operatorname{SK}_1(R)=0,\qquad K_2(R)\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^2.
\]
For odd \(p\), this \(K_2(R)\) ambiguity is killed by the \(p\)-th Hilbert symbol. For \(p=2\), it is killed if \(i\in K\), since the two generators are represented by
\(\{-1,-1\}\) and \(\{-1,t\}\). We therefore obtain a genuine homomorphism
\[
\operatorname{IA}_n\longrightarrow Q. \tag{5}
\]

Choose \(K\) as follows.

* If an odd prime \(p\) divides \(c\), put \(k=c/p\) and take \(\pi\) satisfying
  \[
  \Phi_p(1+\pi^k)=0.
  \]
  This is Eisenstein, and \(v_K(p)=(p-1)k\).
* If \(c\) is a power of two, necessarily \(c\ge4\), take
  \[
  \pi^{c/2}-2\pi^{c/4}+2=0.
  \]
  Then \(v_K(2)=c/2\) and \(i=1-\pi^{c/4}\in K\).

In both cases the critical local-unit pairing gives
\[
(1+\pi,\,1+\pi^{c-1})_p\ne1. \tag{6}
\]

Specialize \(t=1+\pi\). Opposite-root Gaussian factorization of \([A,B_{c-3}]\), using (4), has torus parameter
\[
d=1+s^{c-1};
\]
its remaining root factors have depth at least \(c\). On taking the outer commutator with \(D\), those root factors disappear in \(Q\), because their depth increases to at least \(c+1\). The torus commutator leaves precisely
\[
(t,d)_p^{\pm1}
=(1+\pi,1+\pi^{c-1})_p^{\pm1},
\]
which is nontrivial by (6). Hence \(w_c\) has nontrivial image in \(Q\).

Since \(Q\) has nilpotency class at most \(c\), (5) kills
\(\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)\). Therefore
\[
w_c\notin\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n). \tag{7}
\]

Combining (2), (3), and (7) proves the required strict inclusion for every \(n\ge3,\ c\ge3\). Together with the equality cases,
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D=\mathbb Z_{\ge3}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge3}.}
\]
